text: Where does a card number live, when the payments product must never see one?
prefix: Where does a card number live, when the payments product must never see one?

text: Everything that touches a card number is in P C I D S S scope, the strictest audit in payments.
prefix: Everything that touches a card number is in P C I D S S scope, the strictest audit in payments.

text: So all of it lives in one unit, cards: the card vault, the card frame, and the Uzcard and Humo adapters.
prefix: So all of it lives in one unit, cards: the card vault, the card frame, and the Uzcard and Humo adapters.

text: ecom, the payments product, holds only card tokens and masked numbers, so ecom and any future caller stay out of that scope.
prefix: ecom, the payments product, holds only card tokens and masked numbers, so ecom and any future caller stay out of that scope.

text: The two units share nothing: each has its own database, its own Vault, its own Keycloak and its own monitoring.
prefix: The two units share nothing: each has its own database, its own Vault, its own Keycloak and its own monitoring.

text: Cards never knows its callers: a caller is only a name in cards' inputs, plus a client certificate that cards' own certificate authority signed.
prefix: Cards never knows its callers: a caller is only a name in cards' inputs, plus a client certificate that cards' own certificate authority signed.

text: Another caller, a mobile backend for example, changes cards' inputs, never its code or its deployment.
prefix: Another caller, a mobile backend for example, changes cards' inputs, never its code or its deployment.

text: ecom knows cards only by inputs too: the cards URLs, cards' certificate authority, its own client certificate, and one secret.
prefix: ecom knows cards only by inputs too: the cards URLs, cards' certificate authority, its own client certificate, and one secret.

text: Every call between services is mutual T L S, and it carries a token from cards' own Keycloak with the role the operation needs.
prefix: Every call between services is mutual T L S, and it carries a token from cards' own Keycloak with the role the operation needs.

text: Cards has two doors, and each lets through only what it must.
prefix: Cards has two doors, and each lets through only what it must.

text: The payer door serves only the card frame: the payer's browser loads it and posts the card, and every other path answers four oh four.
prefix: The payer door serves only the card frame: the payer's browser loads it and posts the card, and every other path answers four oh four.

text: Think of a T L S connection as a sealed envelope: S N I is the address written on it, and a certificate is the key that opens it.
prefix: Think of a T L S connection as a sealed envelope: S N I is the address written on it, and a certificate is the key that opens it.

text: The partner door reads only the address, passes the envelope on unopened to the card vault, an adapter or Keycloak, and refuses any address it doesn't know.
prefix: The partner door reads only the address, passes the envelope on unopened to the card vault, an adapter or Keycloak, and refuses any address it doesn't know.

text: ecom gets its certificate the way a person gets a passport.
prefix: ecom gets its certificate the way a person gets a passport.

text: ecom fills in the application, a C S R, with its own private key, which never leaves ecom.
prefix: ecom fills in the application, a C S R, with its own private key, which never leaves ecom.

text: Cards, the passport office, stamps it with its seal and hands back three things: the certificate, cards' own certificate authority to recognise the real cards, and one secret for cards' Keycloak.
prefix: Cards, the passport office, stamps it with its seal and hands back three things: the certificate, cards' own certificate authority to recognise the real cards, and one secret for cards' Keycloak.

text: Each allowed caller has its own roles, its own origins whose pages may embed the frame, and its own session limits.
prefix: Each allowed caller has its own roles, its own origins whose pages may embed the frame, and its own session limits.

text: Fraud limits count refused cards and codes per card, per BIN, per payer address and per risk reference, each within the configured limit and window.
prefix: Fraud limits count refused cards and codes per card, per BIN, per payer address and per risk reference, each within the configured limit and window.

text: Card numbers stay in one unit, behind two narrow doors, and every caller is only an input.
prefix: Card numbers stay in one unit, behind two narrow doors, and every caller is only an input.
